steps.title: The shape is the message
steps.body: Circles give orders. Triangles warn. Rectangles give information.

question.explanation: Triangles warn. Circles give orders, rectangles inform.

a.label: Red ring
a.body: Tells you what you must NOT do — a prohibition.

b.label: Solid blue circle
b.body: Tells you what you MUST do — a positive instruction.

question.prompt: A blue circle showing a white bicycle means…
question.explanation: Blue circles are positive orders — here, a route only pedal cycles may use.

options.text: No speed limit — drive at any speed

question.explanation: It ends local limits: the national limit for your vehicle and road type now applies.

steps.title: The default limits
steps.body: Street lights usually mean 30 mph unless signs say otherwise. Cars: 60 on single carriageways, 70 on duals and motorways.

question.prompt: In a car on a single carriageway at the national limit, your maximum is…
question.explanation: 70 applies to dual carriageways and motorways — single carriageways are 60 for cars.

steps.scene: You turn onto a busy street with lamp posts every few metres. No speed limit signs anywhere.

options.text: It's a 30 mph limit unless signs say otherwise

question.explanation: Street lighting normally means a 30 mph limit applies unless signs show otherwise.

steps.wrongBelief: If the limit is 60, the right speed is 60.

options.text: It isn't wrong — matching the limit keeps traffic flowing
Drivers should always stay exactly 10 mph under the limit
The limit is a maximum — conditions often make a lower speed the safe one

question.explanation: Rule 125: the limit is the absolute maximum — it doesn't make that speed safe.

steps.repairNote: A limit is the legal maximum, not a target. Rain, bends and pedestrians can make 60 dangerous.

steps.scene: A residential street lined with parked cars. A football bounces out between two of them.

options.text: A child may follow the ball — slow down, be ready to stop
Nothing — the road ahead is still clear
The ball may damage your tyres

question.explanation: Where children might be, expect them: ease off and cover the brake.

questions.explanation: Circles order, triangles warn, rectangles inform.

questions.prompt: A white circle with a black diagonal stripe means…

options.text: No limit — any speed is legal

questions.explanation: The stripe ends local limits — the national limit for your vehicle and road applies.

questions.prompt: A car on a dual carriageway under the national limit may not exceed…
questions.explanation: Cars: 70 on dual carriageways and motorways, 60 on single carriageways.

questions.prompt: In heavy rain on a 60 mph road, you should drive…

options.text: At a speed you can stop in safely — often well below 60

questions.explanation: The limit is a maximum, not a promise that the speed is safe in all conditions.

questions.prompt: Passing parked cars on a residential street, you should…

options.text: Expect pedestrians to step out and be ready to stop
Keep at the limit to clear them quickly
Sound your horn as you pass

questions.explanation: Parked cars hide pedestrians — especially children. Slow down and cover the brake.
